ScholarlyArticle.name: An odd-period pedal-antipedal area invariant in elliptic billiards
ScholarlyArticle.headline: An odd-period pedal-antipedal area invariant in elliptic billiards
ScholarlyArticle.description: A signed origin-pedal–antipedal area product is constant for least odd-period elliptic billiards with a strict confocal elliptical caustic.
ScholarlyArticle.abstract: We prove invariant k_{403,a} observed by Reznik, Garcia and Koiller: for every primitive odd-period elliptic billiard family with a strict confocal elliptical caustic, the signed areas of the original orbit's origin pedal and origin antipedal have constant product. All admitted coprime star windings are included, and every real antipedal intersection is finite. A complete pole analysis distinguishes coincident from opposite complex endpoints. Odd-period arithmetic then places the antipedal area and the credited pedal trace in complementary one-dimensional elliptic-function spaces. A direct argument covers circles; an exact four-periodic example rules out dropping the odd restriction.

ScholarlyArticle.name: An odd-period product for focal inversions of outer billiard polygons
ScholarlyArticle.headline: An odd-period product for focal inversions of outer billiard polygons
ScholarlyArticle.description: The signed areas of unit focal inversions of outer tangent polygons have a constant positive product along odd least-period elliptic billiard families.
ScholarlyArticle.abstract: For a periodic billiard family between an ellipse and a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, form the outer polygon by intersecting consecutive tangents at the billiard vertices. Invert its vertices in the unit circles centered at the two original billiard foci, and join successive images by straight segments. We prove that the product of the resulting signed areas is constant for every odd least period, including primitive stars. This proves the invariant conjectured as k904,a in the pinned 2020 list of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller. An explicit inverse-edge factorization reduces the area to a cyclic elliptic sum. Its double principal parts cancel, leaving two simple poles and complementary half-period zeros. The triangular critical case and repeated traversals are included. The analytic methods are classical; no first-proof or absolute-priority claim is made. This AI-assisted research note is unrefereed.

ScholarlyArticle.name: Polynomial compatibility on the Boolean cube from disjoint-support separators
ScholarlyArticle.headline: Polynomial compatibility on the Boolean cube from disjoint-support separators
ScholarlyArticle.abstract: We give an explicit affirmative answer to the two-polynomial question posed by Austrin in Oberwolfach Report 9/2025. Two nonzero real multilinear polynomials of degree at most d on the uniform Boolean cube have a common nonzero vertex whenever every relative coordinate influence is at most 1/(4096d⁸). In fact, disjoint supports force a relative influence at least 1/(1024d⁸). The result is a deduction from the disjoint-support separator of Li–Li–Li–Liu and the covariance inequality of O’Donnell–Saks–Schramm–Servedio, combined with a square-density estimate. We supply the complete deduction and an explicit separator constant. No novelty or first-priority claim is made for this consequence.
ScholarlyArticle.description: An explicit credited deduction: relative coordinate influences at most 1/(4096d⁸) guarantee a common nonzero vertex for two real multilinear polynomials.

ScholarlyArticle.name: Quantitative persistence in a fixed-city area equation
ScholarlyArticle.headline: Quantitative persistence in a fixed-city area equation
ScholarlyArticle.description: Explicit lower bounds keep every city share positive in a fixed weighted-Voronoi area equation when β > 2α, refuting a literal 2007 collapse clause.
ScholarlyArticle.abstract: For finitely many fixed distinct interior sites in the unit square, let each site's positive population share grow at the rate of the area where its influence is maximal, minus its current share. Influence is proportional to population to the power α times distance to the power −β. We prove that every positive initial probability vector gives a global trajectory and, when β > 2α, every share has an explicit positive lower bound for all time. An asymmetric three-site instance with α = 2 and β = 8 has all shares between 1/4096 and 2047/2048. This disproves the unrestricted α > 1 collapse alternative in the literal 2007 fixed-city conjecture. The result is a quantitative, all-site persistence statement; it does not establish convergence or resolve the stochastic city-founding model. We credit the original local geometric mechanism and a directly overlapping 2026 two-city counterexample analysis. No firstness claim is made.
